Formulation
- Predisposing factors: Chronic medical condition (SLE) on immunosuppressant (Methotrexate) increasing vulnerability to infection and health-related worry.
- Precipitating factors: Acute onset (1 day) of cough with haemoptysis, pleuritic right-sided chest pain, fever sensation and increased awareness of heartbeat.
- Perpetuating factors: Ongoing fatigue over two weeks with reduced activity and decreased daily functioning, continued worry about serious diagnoses (e.g., lung cancer).
- Protective factors: Patient sought medical advice, cooperated with remote examination, clinician arranged expedited face-to-face assessment; no acute instability identified.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute health-related anxiety related to recent haemoptysis and chest symptoms
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Attend face-to-face medical assessment today to clarify cause of symptoms and reduce uncertainty/worry
  - Reduce immediate anxiety about serious illness
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Rapidly assess and manage underlying physical cause to reduce anxiety-provoking symptoms
  - Provide reassurance based on examination and investigations; arrange follow-up as indicated
- Actions (Patient):
  - Contact support team / clinic as instructed and attend same-day face-to-face appointment
  - Monitor symptoms and seek urgent care if symptoms worsen (e.g., increased bleeding, marked breathlessness)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange same-day face-to-face review with physical examination (listen to chest), measure blood pressure, pulse, temperature (as arranged in notes)
  - Do not prescribe antibiotics remotely until face-to-face basic assessment completed (per clinician)
  - Consider antibiotic therapy if chest infection confirmed; consider chest X-ray or further investigations if symptoms persist or examination suggests need
  - Provide verbal reassurance that a one-day history with these features is less typical of lung cancer, but follow-up imaging may be needed if not settled

Secondary Problem: Reduced energy / impaired daily functioning
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve energy levels and return to usual activity and exercise as tolerated
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Evaluate for medical causes of fatigue (infection, SLE activity, medication effects) and address reversible causes
- Actions (Patient):
  - Report fatigue and functional impact during face-to-face review; follow clinician advice for rest/activity balance
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Assess for physical contributors during face-to-face assessment; manage acute infection if present and consider further review of SLE management / medication effects as appropriate (not specified in transcript)

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Likely chest infection as a probable cause of current symptoms; lung cancer less likely given acute presentation but may require follow-up imaging if not improving; need for face-to-face assessment and possible antibiotic treatment; reason for not prescribing remotely before clinical examination
